chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'b, from Abu Ubaydah, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the menstruating woman who hears the prostration (verse). He (peace be upon him) said: 'If it is from the obligatory ones, let her prostrate when she hears it.'

key_terms.السَّجْدَة: The prostration (specifically referring to the verse of prostration in the Quran)
key_terms.الْعَزَائِم: The obligatory/determined ones (referring to obligatory prostrations)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a menstruating woman when she hears a verse of prostration in the Quran?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the general prohibition of reciting Quran during menstruation and the specific obligation of prostrating upon hearing the 'azaim (definitive verses of prostration). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the impediment of major ritual impurity (hadath akbar) does not nullify the duty of sajdah, emphasizing the continuity of worship even in states of temporary exclusion from full prayer.
